source.title: Training Matching Pursuit SAEs on LLMs

record.file_problem: The full post is present, but the absorption chart's numerical values are not included in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The post measures SAEBench feature absorption and reports that MP-SAEs fare worse than traditional SAEs, bearing on whether absorption is avoided or remains a problem.
record.gate_note: The post also reports reconstruction, sparse-probing, training-time, decoder-norm, and dead-latent results. These do not measure the feature-splitting or absorption behavior named by the claim versions, so they are not recorded as rows. The absorption chart is referred to but its numeric values are absent from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The post measures the SAEBench feature-absorption rate on Gemma-2-2b layer 12 SAEs. It covers Matching Pursuit SAEs at two L0s and BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs at matched L0s. This is a new SAE family tested on whether absorption persists (V4). It is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author sees no evidence that MP-SAEs reduce absorption; they score much worse than traditional SAEs, likely due to their more expressive encoder, while Matryoshka SAEs score best. The author notes the analysis is not rigorous and the metric could conceivably be invalid for MP-SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Matching Pursuit SAEs with BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs on one model and layer; it does not sweep dictionary size or match the feature-alignment and input-coverage measurements in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The comparison includes two MP-SAE L0 settings (85 and 265) and a static L0=85 variant; the text does not give the individual absorption outcomes by setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Absorption rate depends on SAE architecture and objective. Matryoshka SAEs score best and MP-SAEs worst at matched L0 and width. The author links higher absorption to MP-SAEs' better reconstruction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The degree of feature absorption is set by SAE encoder and objective choice (Matryoshka lowers it; a more expressive MP encoder raises it), not only by size or sparsity.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The author describes the investigation as not rigorous. The absorption metric's numerical results are only in a chart not included in the supplied text, and the post does not directly inspect parent-child firing or input coverage.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows omitted; the reported reconstruction, probing, training-time, decoder-norm, and dead-latent findings do not measure the feature-splitting or absorption behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: Dictionary width is fixed at 32k, so the effect of changing size is not tested. No direct parent/child latent firing inspection is reported beyond the SAEBench metric.
All of V1: no dictionary-size sweep.
All of V2: no splitting analysis.
All of V3: no family or geometry analysis.
All of V5: no cross-size latent decomposition.
All of V6: splitting itself is not measured. Only absorption is compared across objectives.

missing.what: Numeric SAEBench absorption rates per SAE from the absorption chart
missing.locator: Section 'MP-SAEs seem very susceptible to feature absorption' (figure)

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal LessWrong post with one model, one layer, one width and no uncertainty reported. The absorption claims rest on a chart whose values are absent. r6 and r7 were downgraded to cannot_determine because the text gives only a ranking. Reconstruction, probing, training-time and decoder-norm results are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of features across increasing dictionary sizes, their input coverage, or their directions.
No test of splitting at scale or across open SAE releases.
No analysis of nested feature families, geometric proximity, or conceptual hierarchy.

Measures the SAEBench absorption metric, but does not directly show a parent latent failing to fire where a child fires, or establish the detailed parent-child input relationship. Dictionary width is fixed; the post compares L0 settings but does not isolate a general effect of changing SAE size or sparsity.
No decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents or analysis of novel latents.
No direct test that the SAE objective produces splitting on correlated or hierarchical inputs, or that Matryoshka training changes splitting.

relationships.reason: MP-SAEs score much worse than BatchTopK on SAEBench absorption at both L0s. An encoder designed for hierarchy does not remove absorption, and varying L0 doesn't fix it (r1-r3 vs r4-r5). The values are from a chart not in the text.
relationships.display_finding: MP-SAEs scored much worse than BatchTopK on SAEBench absorption at both L0s, so an encoder designed for hierarchy did not remove absorption and changing L0 did not fix it.

relation.reason: The post measures SAEBench absorption for MP-SAEs against BatchTopK and Matryoshka baselines.

tranche.reason: A new SAE family (MP-SAE) on real LLM activations, with an SAEBench absorption result that bears on V4. It argues no version is wrong (it supports V4), so it is not T5.

source_check.notes: All absorption values are in charts that are missing from the text. The text says only that MP-SAEs score much worse than traditional SAEs (BatchTopK and Matryoshka) and that Matryoshka scores best. The author calls it not rigorous and says the metric could conceivably be invalid for MP-SAEs. Each SAE is a single run trained on 300M tokens, with no uncertainty.

statements.problem: none. 'Worse than BatchTopK' follows from the text's 'much worse than traditional SAEs' (BatchTopK and Matryoshka). Per-L0 values are figure-only, as the statement flags.

statements.correction: Gemma-2-2b layer 12, 32k: MP-SAEs (hierarchy-motivated encoder) show no reduction in absorption and score much worse than traditional SAEs (BatchTopK, Matryoshka) on SAEBench absorption. Matryoshka scores best. Values are figure-only; the author calls it not rigorous.
statements.problem: This study is cited for 'hierarchy architectures reduce but do not remove absorption'. But the text says MP-SAEs do not reduce absorption; they score much worse than traditional SAEs. The per-study line itself is accurate.

none. Model, layer, width, L0s, 'real LLM activations', 'not rigorous' and 'figure-only' all match the text. The author's caveat that the metric might be invalid for MP-SAEs is omitted; he says he can't see why it would be.

reader_labels.reason: The post says MP-SAEs score much worse on the feature-absorption metric than traditional SAEs, consistent with absorption remaining a problem (r1-r3). It reports Matryoshka SAEs as best on the metric (r6-r7). The chart values are unavailable, and the metric does not directly establish the stated parent-child firing pattern.
